subject: Re: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options (Post-demo recap)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options (Post-demo recap)

Hi Elena / Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key encryption and key management items we discussed and outline next steps so your security and procurement teams have what they need.

Recap of requirements you surfaced:
- In-transit encryption: TLS 1.2+ required for all endpoints, mTLS for private connectors (Paywise standard).
- At-rest encryption: all customer data must be encrypted at rest with 256-bit AES or equivalent.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): Paywise prefers customer-managed KMS/HSM keys for primary data encryption keys and requires key rotation policies and export controls.
- Audit & logging: request for detailed key usage logs, key rotation history, and access audit trails for the encryption keys that protect Paywise data.
- Data residency: production data stored in us-west-2; ability to pin region for logs/archives.
- Retention controls / PII handling: support for configurable data retention windows and deletion upon request.

What Redwood supports (high level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 by default, TLS 1.2 supported; we can enable mTLS on Private deployments and VPC connectors.
- At-rest: All hosted and dedicated volumes are encrypted at rest. For Hosted API we use provider-managed encryption by default; Dedicated and Private offer CMK options.
- CMK options:
  * Hosted API (customer-managed KMS): we offer integration with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) where you can bring your own key for encrypting storage buckets and backups.
  * Dedicated / Private: full BYOK/HSM support; keys can be stored in your KMS/HSM and Redwood can be configured to use those keys; HSM-backed key wrapping available for enterprise customers.
- Audit logs: We can provide key usage logs and operator audit logs (exportable to your logging pipeline or delivered to an S3 bucket in your account).
- Data residency: region pinning supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can choose region where supported.

Attachments I'm including: SOC2 report (redacted), our KMS integration guide, and a short DAP (data access/privacy) intake spreadsheet you can forward to your security team.

Next steps / asks:
1) Elena / Jordan: confirm whether Paywise needs HSM-backed keys or if a managed KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) CMK is sufficient.
2) Security: if HSM is required, please share any vendor-specific policies or certs we should validate (FIPS, PCI modules, etc.).
3) Procurement: if Paywise wants CMK on Hosted, we'll need org-level KMS ARN/credentials for the integration and a short network/access checklist.
4) Redwood: will prepare a short design note (1-2 pages) mapping Paywise requirements to our Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and include operational steps for key rotation and log delivery.

I've cc'd Nikhil (SE) and Rishi (Security) who will join any follow-up calls and can provide implementation details.

Thanks — available for a 30-45 minute follow-up next week if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Director | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the detailed note and the attachments, very helpful. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) CMK requirement: Our security team would prefer HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 level 3) for primary data encryption keys.
2) Key rotation: we require the ability to rotate keys annually and to see rotation metadata in logs (timestamp, actor, key ID).
3) Exportability: We need to confirm whether Redwood ever has access to plaintext keys or whether keys remain non-exportable by design.
4) Audit logs: we'd like a sample of the key-usage log format (timestamps, API call names, request IDs) so our SIEM team can onboard it.

From procurement: please also include a short checklist of network requirements if we move to Dedicated or Private (VPC peering, IP allowlists, egress rules).

Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up with your security engineer this Thursday morning (our time)? If so, Jordan will pick a time.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Garcia
Head of Security Engineering | Paywise
elena.garcia@paywise.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@paywise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options (Post-demo recap)

Elena — great questions. Quick answers from an SE/implementation perspective: 

- HSM-backed keys: Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API we can integrate with your KMS and reference HSM-backed keys, but the control plane components are still managed by Redwood; we can ensure keys are non-exportable and wrapped so Redwood does not see plaintext keys. For the highest assurance (full separation), our Private deployment with customer-managed control plane in your VPC is recommended.

- Key rotation metadata: We can push rotation events and key-version metadata to an S3 bucket or into your SIEM via our log delivery pipeline. The payload contains key_id, rotation_timestamp, operator_identity (IAM principal), and rotation_reason (if provided).

- Access to plaintext keys: We do not hold plaintext encryption keys in our control plane. Key operations are performed via your KMS/HSM (Encrypt/Decrypt/Wrap/Unwrap) using API calls. For Hosted CMK integrations we request limited encrypt/decrypt permissions scoped to service key usage; these operations never return raw key material.

- Sample log: attaching a sanitized sample log format in the KMS guide (see redwood-kms-integration-guide.pdf).

If you confirm you need FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM, we'll prepare an architecture note that shows where the key material lives, how the key operations occur, and the audit/logging endpoints.

I'm available Thursday 10:00-12:00 PT for a quick call.

Thanks,
